tagline: Below the gold camps, into a park named partly for sheep.
intro: Below Julian, Highway 78 leaves town as Banner Road and runs past the old gold camp of Banner to Scissors Crossing, where County Route S2 crosses it in the San Felipe Valley. Shortly after, the road enters Anza-Borrego Desert State Park and keeps to it for about eighteen miles, out past Ocotillo Wells. Banner sits at 2,743 feet. Ocotillo Wells sits at 163.

The park, the largest state park in California, is named for the explorer Juan Bautista de Anza and for borrego, the Spanish word for sheep. The way down was once harder. Before the Banner toll road opened, miners' supplies were lowered by hand down a 1,000-foot slope.

moments.title: San Felipe Valley
moments.text: From 1858 the Butterfield Overland Mail kept its San Felipe Station in this valley, headquarters for twelve stage stations strung between Warner's Ranch and Fort Yuma.

moments.title: Ocotillo Wells
moments.text: A desert community with a dirt-runway airport, where down Split Mountain Road the Iron Door bar keeps decorated dollar bills stapled to its walls in layers.
